requirements.businessContext: JPL-Leagues uses a single sign-in form to authenticate three distinct identity types — superadmin, league admin, and team — backed by an HMAC-SHA256 signed cookie with a 7-day TTL. The same endpoint handles all three because the identifier itself decides the path (email vs. team login ID). Forced password changes and first-login profile setup are enforced server-side via redirect hints in the sign-in response. Middleware classifies every /api/* request as public, admin-only, team-only, or cron, and applies rate limiting to credential and expensive-compute endpoints.

businessRules.rule: Sign-in requires both `identifier` and `password` in the request body; either missing returns 400 'Login ID and password are required'.
An identifier containing '@' routes to the admin (users table) path; otherwise it routes to the team (teams.teamLoginId) path.
Admin email lookup is case-folded to lowercase before the database query; team login IDs are matched exact-case (no normalization).
Invalid identifier OR wrong password both return 401 with the generic message 'Invalid credentials' — never distinguish between the two.
Successful sign-in sets a session cookie named `session` containing a base64url-encoded payload `{id,type,exp}` plus a `.<hexSig>` HMAC-SHA256 signature.
Session TTL is exactly 7 days (60*60*24*7 = 604800 seconds), encoded into the payload's `exp` field at issue time.
SESSION_SECRET must be at least 32 characters; missing or shorter throws 'SESSION_SECRET environment variable must be set (min 32 characters)' on first sign/verify attempt.
Session verification uses constant-time signature comparison (XOR-accumulation loop) to avoid timing attacks.
Session cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, path=/, maxAge=604800; `secure` is set only when NODE_ENV=production.
Admin sign-in `redirectTo` resolves as: mustChangePassword → /change-password; otherwise role='superadmin' → /superadmin; role='admin' → /admin.
Team sign-in `redirectTo` resolves as: mustChangePassword → /change-password; else !isProfileComplete → /setup; else /dashboard.
Change-password requires `currentPassword` and `newPassword` in the body; missing either returns 400 'Current password and new password are required'.
New password must be at least 8 characters; failure returns 400 'New password must be at least 8 characters'.

New password must contain at least one digit or special character matching the class [\d!@#$%^&*()_+\-=\[\]{};':"\\|,.<>/?]; failure returns 400 'New password must contain at least one number or special character'.
Change-password requires a valid session cookie; missing OR invalid signature returns 401 'Not authenticated' (the route itself enforces this; middleware would also reject it).
Wrong currentPassword on change-password returns 401 'Current password is incorrect' (and the password is NOT rotated).
Successful change-password sets mustChangePassword=false and updatedAt on the user/team row and persists a bcrypt hash (cost factor 10) of the new password.
Team change-password redirectTo equals '/' when isProfileComplete is true; '/setup' when false (re-fetched after the update).
Admin change-password redirectTo equals '/superadmin' for role='superadmin'; '/admin' otherwise. (It does NOT use the team /setup path.)
Sign-out clears the session cookie by writing an empty value with maxAge=0 and path=/; the response is always 200 with `{success:true,message:'Signed out'}`.
Sign-out is idempotent — calling POST /api/auth/signout without a session cookie still returns 200 and does not error.
Every /api/auth/* path is treated as public by middleware (no session required to invoke any of them — auth, signout, me).
/api/auth/me returns 200 with `{authenticated:false}` for missing, invalid, expired, or otherwise unrecognised tokens — it NEVER returns 401.

/api/auth/me with a valid admin/superadmin session returns `{authenticated:true, type, adminLeagueId, leagueSlug, user:{id,email,name,role,isAdmin:true}}`. adminLeagueId is null for superadmin (no league join performed).
/api/auth/me populates `leagueSlug` only when the admin is assigned to exactly one league; for two or more leagues, leagueSlug is null (although adminLeagueId is still set to the first row).

/api/auth/me with a valid team session returns `{authenticated:true, type:'team', leagueFormat, leagueSlug, clubAuctionEnabled, auctionTier, team:{id,name,groupId,mustChangePassword,isProfileComplete}}`.
/api/auth/me has a defensive fallback when the auction_tier column is missing (pending migration) — the inner SELECT is retried without that column and auctionTier defaults to 'complete'.
/api/auth/me defaults leagueFormat to 'tvt' and clubAuctionEnabled to false when the league row is missing or those columns are null.
Rate limit: POST /api/auth/signin allows 5 attempts per IP per 60s; the 6th request returns 429 'Too many requests. Please try again later.'.
Rate limit: POST /api/auth/change-password allows 5 attempts per IP per 60s; the 6th request returns 429.
Rate limit: POST /api/admin/<leagueId>/reset-season allows 1 attempt per IP per 60s; the 2nd request returns 429.

Per-admin rate limit: POSTs to expensive admin endpoints (generate-playoffs, generate-brackets, advance-playoffs, create-gameweeks, process-all/league-gw) are capped at 30 per session ID per 60s; over-limit returns 429 'Too many requests on this endpoint. Please slow down.'.
Rate limiter fails open: if Upstash Redis is not configured (UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL/_TOKEN missing) OR Redis throws, all requests proceed unblocked.
Client IP for rate-limit keys is taken from x-forwarded-for (first hop), falling back to x-real-ip, then literal 'unknown'.
Cron secret bypass: requests to /api/cron/* OR /api/admin/* carrying `Authorization: Bearer <CRON_SECRET>` are allowed through with response headers x-session-id='cron' and x-session-type='admin'.

When CRON_SECRET is set but the request to /api/cron/* presents no/wrong bearer header, middleware returns 401 'Unauthorized'. When CRON_SECRET is unset, /api/cron/* returns 500 'CRON_SECRET not configured'.
Admin API routes (/api/admin/*, and POST to /api/gameweeks/<n>) require session.type ∈ {admin, superadmin}; team session returns 403 'Admin access required'.
Team API routes (/api/team/*) require session.type='team'; admin/superadmin returns 403 'Team access required'.
Any other /api/* route not classified as public/admin/team still requires a valid session, but accepts either admin or team session type.

Public read-only endpoints accessible without a session via GET: /api/auth/signin, /api/auth/signout, /api/auth/me, /api/fixtures, /api/standings, /api/playoffs/bracket, /api/playoffs/winners, /api/leagues, /api/continental-championship/cup-standings, and /api/gameweeks/<numeric>.

Middleware forwards verified session into downstream handlers via x-session-id and x-session-type response headers. For /api/admin/<leagueId>/* routes, x-league-id is also extracted from the path and forwarded.
Middleware only runs on paths under /api/* (matcher='/api/:path*'); page routes like /signin and /change-password are NOT gated by middleware.
Sign-in admin response body shape: `{success, user:{id,email,name,role,isAdmin:true,mustChangePassword}, redirectTo}`; the sign-in client trusts data.redirectTo verbatim.
Sign-in team response body shape: `{success, team:{id,name,groupId,isAdmin:false,mustChangePassword,isProfileComplete}, redirectTo}` (no `user` field).
Sign-in fallback redirect on the client: if data.redirectTo is missing, the client navigates to '/admin' when data.user exists, else '/dashboard'.
Change-password client requires confirmPassword to equal newPassword; mismatch shows 'New passwords do not match' and never calls the API.

Change-password client length check requires newPassword.length >= 8 with message 'New password must be at least 8 characters'; this mirrors the server's 8-char requirement (BR-AUTH-013) so the user receives an inline error before submission and no API call fires for shorter passwords.

Change-password client validates the digit/special character requirement locally using the same character class as the server (/[\d!@#$%^&*()_+\-=\[\]{};':"\\|,.<>\/?]/); a password missing a digit/special is blocked client-side with message 'New password must contain at least one number or special character' before any API call, mirroring the server rule (BR-AUTH-014).
On successful change-password, the client displays a green success banner and redirects to data.redirectTo (or '/') after a 2-second setTimeout.
Sign-in client submit button is disabled while a request is in-flight and the label changes to 'Signing in...' to prevent double-submit.
Sign-in client error UI: a red banner appears with the server's error text on any non-2xx response; on network failure the banner shows 'Network error. Please try again.'.
Session token format: two dot-separated parts only; any other shape (zero or two or more dots) fails verifySession and returns null.
verifySession returns null whenever payload is missing any of id/type/exp, or if exp is in the past (epoch seconds compared to Math.floor(Date.now()/1000)).
Sign-in catch-all: unexpected server errors return 500 with body `{error:'Sign in failed'}` (the inner exception is logged but not exposed).
Change-password catch-all: unexpected server errors return 500 with body `{error:'Failed to change password'}`.

gapFlags.issue: Change-password client min-length is 6 chars (src/app/change-password/page.tsx:26-30) but the server enforces 8 chars (src/app/api/auth/change-password/route.ts:32-37). Per BR-AUTH-047 the server is authoritative, so a user typing a 6- or 7-char password sees the client pass validation and then receives a 400 banner from the server — confusing UX and a likely defect. Need product owner to confirm the intended minimum (8 vs 6) and align both layers. NOT a sign-off blocker — tracked here as a documentation/follow-up item. Regression coverage is pinned by TC-AUTH-086 and TC-AUTH-087 so the current behaviour is locked in until the discrepancy is resolved.
gapFlags.resolution: Resolved 2026-05-25 via DEF-AUTH-001 fix: client validation in src/app/change-password/page.tsx now matches the server — min-length raised from 6 to 8 and a char-class regex (digit or special character matching the server's class) was added, so the user sees an inline error before submit instead of the post-submit 400 banner. Server (authoritative) was untouched. BR-AUTH-047 and BR-AUTH-048 now describe the OLD client behaviour and need a BA update; pinning TC-AUTH-086 and TC-AUTH-087 will now fail and need QA re-authoring against the new aligned behaviour.

defects.title: Change-password page client validation diverges from API (min length 6 vs 8, no digit/special check)
defects.description: The /change-password page (src/app/change-password/page.tsx:26) enforces a 6-character minimum and only checks confirmPassword match. The API (src/app/api/auth/change-password/route.ts:32-44) enforces an 8-character minimum AND requires at least one digit or special character. A user submitting a 6- or 7-char password — or an 8+ char letters-only password — passes the client check and receives a 400 banner from the server with no advance warning.
defects.expectedBehaviour: Client validation matches API: newPassword.length >= 8 AND contains at least one digit or special character. User receives an inline error before submit.
defects.actualBehaviour: Client only checks length >= 6 and confirm-match. Server rejects with a 400 the user has no advance warning about.
defects.notes: Two paths to fix: (a) raise client min to 8 + add char-class regex; (b) drop server min to 6 + remove char-class requirement. Per BR-AUTH-047 the server is authoritative — option (a) is the lower-risk fix. [DEV 2026-05-25] Applied option (a) in src/app/change-password/page.tsx:26-36 — raised client min-length from 6 to 8 and added the same char-class regex the server uses (/[\d!@#$%^&*()_+\-=\[\]{};':"\\|,.<>\/?]/). Confirm-match check unchanged. Server (authoritative) untouched. Self-verified: tsc clean for the touched file (pre-existing unrelated errors in tests/league-types/*.spec.ts only); manual diff review clean — inline errors now fire before submit so the user no longer sees a post-submit 400 banner for these two rules. Awaiting QA re-run of pinningTestCases. [QA] TC-AUTH-086 and TC-AUTH-087 currently PIN the OLD (defective) client behaviour and will now FAIL — re-author them against the new aligned behaviour: a 6-char password should be blocked client-side with 'New password must be at least 8 characters' and no API call should fire; an 8+ char letters-only password should be blocked client-side with 'New password must contain at least one number or special character' and no API call should fire. Confirm AC-AUTH-048 wording matches the fix. [BA] BR-AUTH-047 and BR-AUTH-048 now describe the OLD client behaviour and need rewording: BR-AUTH-047 should state the client min-length is 8 (matches server, BR-AUTH-013); BR-AUTH-048 should state the client now DOES validate the digit/special-character requirement locally (matches server, BR-AUTH-014). AC-AUTH-048's 'CODE-CONFIRMED: may be a defect' suffix and its expected-result text should be updated to reflect that the client now rejects 6-char passwords before any API call. [QA-VERIFIED]: 2026-05-25 — TC-AUTH-086 + TC-AUTH-087 inverted; client/server password rules aligned. [BA-UPDATED]: 2026-05-25 — BR-AUTH-047 + BR-AUTH-048 + AC-AUTH-048 updated.
defects.resolution: Raised the client-side min-length from 6 to 8 and added a digit/special-character regex check in src/app/change-password/page.tsx:26-36, matching the server rules in src/app/api/auth/change-password/route.ts:32-44. The confirm-match check is preserved. Inline errors now appear before the form is submitted, eliminating the confusing post-submit 400 banner the user previously received. Chose option (a) from the defect notes (raise client to match server) because BR-AUTH-047 marks the server as authoritative — lower-risk than relaxing server rules.
